nativeOutcome: One additional participant modeled to cross a 0.5 standard-deviation loneliness-improvement threshold at 12 months
decision: Do not publish a dollars-per-10-QALYs price. Curry did not directly observe the native responder outcome: MFI constructs it by combining a judgmental 0.5-SD threshold, a normal change-score distribution, and a judgmental causal discount applied to an uncontrolled pre/post study. The available health-utility literature does not map this modeled threshold crossing to a preference-based utility gain, and neither onset nor persistence is measured.

candidateEvidence.design: Systematic review of 19 observational studies reporting loneliness or social isolation alongside health-state utility values
candidateEvidence.population: People with pre-existing health conditions; populations, conditions, loneliness measures, and utility instruments varied
candidateEvidence.contrast: Lonely versus not lonely in two chronic-condition studies using HUI2 or EQ-5D-3L
candidateEvidence.candidateArithmetic: 0.04 annual utility gap x 1 assumed year
candidateEvidence.boundary: The 0.04 difference is a cross-sectional association between binary loneliness states in other populations. It is not a mapping from a 0.5-SD change, a validated Curry responder threshold, a causal effect of Senior Vitality, or a measured one-year utility gain.

failedGates.label: Validate the native responder outcome
failedGates.why: Curry reported an average pre/post change, not the share of participants crossing a responder threshold. MFI imposes a 0.5-SD threshold and standard-normal change distribution, so the native denominator itself is modeled rather than observed or clinically validated.

failedGates.label: Map the score change to utility
failedGates.why: No validated mapping was located from Curry's loneliness measure or MFI's 0.5-SD modeled threshold to EQ-5D, HUI, SF-6D, AQoL, or another preference-based utility instrument. A binary lonely-versus-not-lonely contrast is not interchangeable with a standardized score change.

failedGates.label: Separate loneliness from correlated illness
failedGates.why: The candidate 0.04 utility gap is observational and comes from people with pre-existing health conditions. Depression, disability, chronic illness, and other confounding can affect both loneliness and utility, so the association cannot be treated as the utility caused by reducing loneliness.

failedGates.label: Measure Senior Vitality's causal effect
failedGates.why: The Curry study had no concurrent comparison group, used convenience and referral recruitment, and retained 90 of 106 baseline participants at 12 months. The model's 0.08-SD causal shift is a judgmental one-third attribution of the observed 0.24-SD change; null or harm remains plausible.

failedGates.label: Establish timing and persistence
failedGates.why: A 12-month endpoint does not establish when loneliness or health utility changed, the area under the utility curve during the year, or whether any benefit persisted beyond the final assessment.

failedGates.label: Identify the active component and utility instrument
failedGates.why: Senior Vitality bundles devices, connectivity, classes, tutoring, social contact, and health coaching, so the active component is unknown. Curry did not collect preference-based utility, and evidence reviews warn that common instruments such as EQ-5D may miss psychosocial change.

illustrativeCounterfactual.assumptions: If, contrary to the missing evidence, every modeled 0.5-SD threshold crossing caused the full 0.04 annual utility difference for exactly one year, assign 0.04 QALY per modeled improvement.
illustrativeCounterfactual.publicationBoundary: This arithmetic is shown only to expose the unsupported responder, mapping, causality, and duration assumptions. It must not appear as Curry's comparison price, rank, or recommendation.

requiredEvidence: Pre-specify and validate a participant-level loneliness response threshold before analyzing the next cohort.
Collect a preference-based utility measure alongside the loneliness instrument at baseline, intermediate time points, 12 months, and follow-up.
Use a randomized or credible concurrent comparison with complete participant flow, exposure, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Estimate utility and loneliness change jointly so the bridge does not rely on a cross-study standardized-score mapping.
Measure onset, area under the utility curve, persistence, active program components, incremental cost, public-funding displacement, capacity, and a dated marginal funding plan.
